newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia rebels warn of obstacles to troop handover.
newsitem.headline: Colombia rebels warn of obstacles to troop handover.

text.p: Leftist rebels warned in a communique on Sunday that undercover military operations in the southern jungles of Colombia could hamper the release of 60 soldiers they have been holding prisoner for the last nine months.

The three-point statement issued by Revolutionary Armed Forces of Colombia (FARC) guerrillas said all government troops had been pulled out of a 5,000 square mile (13,000 sq km) zone of Caqueta province as agreed but said some had returned posing as street vendors.

President Ernesto Samper ordered all army units out of the area for 32 days -- a process that began 10 days ago -- to allow the FARC to hand over 60 soldiers seized in neighbouring Putumayo province on Aug. 30.
"The demilitarization of the zone has be accomplished. Our units have verified that," FARC commanders said in a communique issued to reporters in Caqueta.

"But some of the soldiers that left the zone have returned to (the town of) Cartagena del Chaira dressed as civilians and posing as street vendors. If the armed forces do not fulfil Samper's orders to the letter they will be responsible for any delays in the handover of the prisoners," the communique added.

Gen. Agustin Ardila, commander of the army's Fourth Division who is overseeing the troop pullout, was unavailable for comment on the FARC claims that undercover troops had filtered back into the area.

The attack on the Las Delicias base, in which the 60 soldiers were captured and at least 27 other killed, marked the start of one of the bloodiest rebel offensives in three decades of guerrilla war and the beginning of Latin America's longest-running hostage crisis -- largely overshadowed by the recent rebel siege of the Japanese embassy residence in Lima.
Under the terms of the demilitarization deal the army was allowed five days to retreat and the FARC was given a further five days to check the withdrawal was complete.

FARC negotiators are due to meet with government representatives and international observers on Monday and Tuesday to finalise details for the release of the soldiers, together with another 10 marines captured in fighting in northwest Choco province in January.
If all goes according to plan the rebels would then release their prisoners some time in the next two weeks.
A partial demilitarization of Caqueta province in December failed to win the release of the soldiers when the guerrillas said troops remained in the area and had prepared ambushes for them.
